title: Quantifying Inefficiency
abstract: arXiv:2412.11984v4 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: We axiomatically define a cardinal social inefficiency function, which, given alternatives and individuals' vNM preferences, assigns a number -- the social inefficiency -- to each alternative. These numbers induce not only an ordinal comparison but also a cardinal comparison between alternatives that is uniquely defined by our axioms despite no exogenously given interpersonal comparison, outside option, or disagreement point. We interpret these numbers as per-capita losses in endogenously normalized utility. We apply our social inefficiency function to a setting where interpersonal comparison is hard to justify -- object allocation without money -- leveraging techniques from computer science to prove an approximate-efficiency result for the Random Serial Dictatorship mechanism.

translated_abstract: arXiv:2412.11984v4 公告类型：替换 摘要：我们公理化地定义了一个基数社会无效率函数，该函数在给定备选方案和个体的vNM偏好时，为每个备选方案分配一个数字——社会无效率。这些数字不仅引出了备选方案之间的序数比较，还引出了基数比较，且这种比较由我们的公理唯一确定，尽管没有外生给定的人际比较、外部选项或分歧点。我们将这些数字解释为内生化归一化效用下的人均损失。我们将我们的社会无效率函数应用于一个难以合理进行人际比较的设定——无货币的物品分配——利用计算机科学的技术，证明了随机独裁机制的一个近似效率结果。
tldr: 本文提出一种公理化定义的基数社会无效率函数，无需人际比较即可唯一量化备选方案的无效率，并应用于无货币分配中证明随机独裁机制的近似效率。
en_tdlr: This paper axiomatically defines a cardinal social inefficiency function that uniquely quantifies inefficiency without interpersonal comparison, and applies it to prove approximate efficiency of Random Serial Dictatorship in object allocation without money.
